## Setup required: Telegram chat ID (always, no exceptions)

This workflow is cron-triggered, *i.e.*, there is no incoming Telegram message to derive a chat ID from, so the placeholder `YOUR_TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID` in its Telegram nodes MUST be replaced with a real value before it can send anything at all, in every run, not just for testing.

**How to find your chat ID:**
1. Message this template's bot at least once (any text).
2. Open **JobOps Template Bot Router** → click the **JobOps Template Bot Trigger** node → **Listen for test event**.
3. Send another message to the bot.
4. n8n captures the incoming update — find `message.chat.id` in the output panel. That's your chat ID.
5. Paste it into every `YOUR_TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID` field in this workflow's Telegram nodes (Send Follow-up Reminder, Send Interview Prep Reminder, Send Deadline Reminder).

**Important:** this workflow is left published/live with the placeholder still in place.
It will run on its schedule and fail (harmlessly) until you fill in a real ID. 
After editing the chat ID fields, you must **republish this workflow** for the change to take effect.
Editing alone only updates the draft, not what's actually running.

## Setup required: jobops_template_config Data Table ID (always, no exceptions)

This workflow looks up the Airtable base/table IDs it needs from an n8n Data Table (D-24) rather than hardcoding them or using n8n Variables (gated behind a paid plan). The placeholder `YOUR_JOBOPS_TEMPLATE_CONFIG_DATA_TABLE_ID` in every **Load Config** node (Follow-up, Interview, Deadline) MUST be replaced with your own Data Table's ID before this workflow can do anything, in every run, not just for testing.

**How to set it up:**
1. Create a Data Table in your n8n instance (Data Tables → New), name it `jobops_template_config`.
2. Add one row with a column for every base/table ID your own Airtable base uses (baseId, tableApplications, tableInterviews).
3. Open each of the three **Load Config** nodes in this workflow → click into the Data Table field → select your new table. This replaces the placeholder with your table's real ID in all three.

**Important:** this workflow is left published/live with the placeholder still in place. It will run on its schedule and fail (harmlessly) until you fill in your real Data Table ID. After editing it, you must **republish this workflow** for the change to take effect — editing alone only updates the draft, not what's actually running.
